title: Boolean junta approximation from energy bounds
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$ on its outcome space. For a coordinate set $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, an integer $k\ge 0$, and real numbers $a,b$, suppose the total expected squared component energy over sets $S$ with $|S|>k$ is at most $a$, and the corresponding total over sets with $|S|\le k$ but $S\nsubseteq J$ is at most $b$. Then there is a function $g$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$, depending only on coordinates in $J$, such that $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le a+b$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$J$ is a subset of the coordinate set
component energy above degree $k$ is at most $a$
component energy of degree at most $k$ on sets not contained in $J$ is at most $b$
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, $J\subseteq[n]$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $a,b\in\mathbb R$. If $\sum_{|S|>k}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2\le a$ and $\sum_{|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2\le b$, then there exists $g:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ with $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le a+b$.
